verdict.rationale: Flagsmith documents every agent write path the story names: an Admin/Management API covering everything the dashboard can do, an official CLI for managing flags, and an official MCP server that lets agents manage flags in IDE or CI/CD sessions. It also documents four-eyes Change Requests with a configurable number of required approvals, plus RBAC to limit who can modify production. What is not documented is that writes made through the API, CLI or MCP are actually forced into Change Requests rather than applied directly, so the core 'force my changes through approval' guarantee for agents is only implied. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that Admin API/MCP/CLI writes to approval-gated environments are routed into Change Requests, how agent credentials map to RBAC/approval rules, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI agent, I can create and toggle flags through documented APIs, CLIs, or MCP — and the platform can force my changes through approval workflows instead of letting me write to production unreviewed

citations.quote: Anything you can do in the Flagsmith dashboard, you can also do via the Admin API.
Your assistant can manage feature flags, segments, multivariate options, and release workflows on your behalf — in a human-in-the-loop IDE session, or fully automated in a CI/CD pipeline.
The Flagsmith CLI lets you manage flags, segments, features, projects and environments from your terminal
Feature Change Requests help creating a four-eyes workflow (create, approve, publish) to updating feature flags, similarly to Pull Requests in GitHub.
Select the required number of approvals for each Change Request to be applied.
Only allow certain users to modify your production environments.
